meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.title: Everolimus for advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (RADIANT-3)
data.authors: Yao JC; Shah MH; Ito T; Bohas CL; Wolin EM; et al.; Oberg K

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: A phase 3 RCT (n=410) that made everolimus a standard treatment for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. It more than doubled progression-free survival (11.0 vs 4.6 months, a 65% reduction in risk of progression/death) with mostly mild side effects. Another FDA-approved indication built on blocking mTOR.
data.abstract_excerpt:
Everolimus, an oral inhibitor of mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), has shown antitumor activity in patients with advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, in two phase 2 studies. We evaluated the agent in a prospective, randomized, phase 3 study.

We randomly assigned 410 patients who had advanced, low-grade or intermediate-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors with radiologic progression within the previous 12 months to receive everolimus, at a dose of 10 mg once daily (207 patients), or placebo (203 patients), both in conjunction with best supportive care.

extracted_findings.effect: Everolimus prolonged progression-free survival in advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
extracted_findings.dose: Everolimus 10 mg once daily vs placebo; oral; international multicenter double-blind phase 3 (RADIANT-3).
extracted_findings.sample_size: 410 patients, 82 centers, 18 countries (target 392) with advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
extracted_findings.effect_size: Everolimus prolonged progression-free survival vs placebo (primary endpoint). Confirmed objective responses 5% (everolimus) vs 2% (placebo).
extracted_findings.limitations: Noninfectious pneumonitis / interstitial lung disease in 7 patients (5 drug-related, ~2%); other cancer therapies debated as comparators.
